paragraphs.title: The Order to Count Israel and Joab’s Objection

answers: Joab
Satan
Gad
easy.explanation: Verse 1 says, “Satan stood up against Israel, and provoked David to number Israel.”
easy.q: Who stood up against Israel and provoked David to number the people?

answers: Joab and the rulers of the people
Gad and Ornan
The elders only
easy.explanation: David told Joab and the rulers of the people to count Israel.
easy.q: To whom did David give the command to number Israel?

answers: Judah and Simeon
Reuben and Gad
Levi and Benjamin
easy.explanation: The passage says that Joab did not count Levi and Benjamin.
easy.q: Which two tribes did Joab not count?

answers: He did not want to leave Jerusalem
He saw the command as a cause of trespass to Israel
He did not know how to count the people
medium.explanation: Joab asked why David would require the census and become a cause of trespass to Israel.
medium.q: Why did Joab object to David’s command?

answers: He carried out the command only partially
He completely refused to number the people
He asked David to give up the throne
medium.explanation: Joab went throughout Israel and counted the people, but he did not count Levi and Benjamin.
medium.q: What did Joab do despite his objection?

answers: Done quickly
Completely forgotten
Hateful or detestable
medium.explanation: “Abominable” describes something greatly hated or detested.
medium.q: What does the word “abominable” mean in the statement that the king’s word was abominable to Joab?

answers: He carried out the command without objection
His objection was shown in his actions as well as his words
He forgot the names of the tribes
challenge.explanation: Joab objected to the census and expressed that objection by carrying it out only partially.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from Joab’s failure to count Levi and Benjamin?

answers: Satan’s provocation led to David’s command, and the command led to a partial census
Joab provoked David, and David refused to act
The command was given after the census was completed
challenge.explanation: Satan provoked David, David ordered the census, and Joab carried it out only partly.
challenge.q: What relationship between Satan’s action, David’s command, and Joab’s work is shown in these verses?

answers: The people did not belong to the king
The people were already the king’s servants, so Joab questioned the need to number them
The people were unable to fight
challenge.explanation: Joab said that the people were all David’s servants and questioned why the king required the census.
challenge.q: What do Joab’s words emphasize about David’s relationship to the people?

paragraphs.title: The Sin, the Plague, and David’s Choice of Punishment

answers: He confessed his sin and asked for forgiveness
He blamed Joab alone
He fled from Jerusalem
easy.explanation: David said, “I have sinned greatly,” and asked God to take away his iniquity.
easy.q: How did David respond after he realized that he had sinned?

answers: Joab
Ornan
Gad
easy.explanation: The LORD spoke to Gad, David’s seer, and Gad delivered the message to David.
easy.q: Who told David about the three possible punishments?

answers: Seventy thousand
Four hundred seventy thousand
One hundred thousand
easy.explanation: The passage says that seventy thousand men of Israel fell.
easy.q: How many people died in the plague?

answers: War, exile, and famine
Three years of famine, three months of pursuit, or three days of the LORD’s sword and pestilence
Another census, tribute, and war
medium.explanation: Gad offered three years of famine, three months before David’s foes, or three days of the LORD’s sword and pestilence.
medium.q: What were the three punishments offered to David?

answers: Because he knew that God’s mercies were very great
Because he wanted to escape all punishment
Because he did not understand the choices
medium.explanation: David said, “Very great are his mercies,” and therefore chose the LORD’s hand.
medium.q: Why did David choose to fall into the hand of the LORD rather than into the hand of man?

answers: I have won
I have acted foolishly
I have been punished
medium.explanation: David was admitting that his action had been foolish and seriously wrong.
medium.q: What does David mean when he says, “I have done very foolishly”?

answers: He asked that the punishment fall on him and his house rather than on the people
He asked that only the people be punished
He denied responsibility for the census
challenge.explanation: David accepted responsibility and asked that the people not be plagued for his sin.
challenge.q: What does David’s request, “Let thine hand…be on me, and on my father’s house,” show?

answers: The angel moved from Ornan’s threshing floor to Gibeon
The LORD stopped the angel before he destroyed Jerusalem
David stopped the plague by his own power
challenge.explanation: The LORD told the destroying angel to stop, saying, “It is enough, stay now thine hand.”
challenge.q: What change occurred during the plague?

answers: He denied that the census had happened
He moved from committing the act to confessing guilt and asking for mercy
He claimed that Joab was king
challenge.explanation: David confessed his sin, acknowledged that he had done evil, and pleaded for mercy on the people.
challenge.q: How does David’s response develop after the census?

paragraphs.title: The Altar at Ornan’s Threshing Floor and the Purchase of the Site

answers: At the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite
At Gibeon
At Joab’s house
easy.explanation: Gad told David to set up an altar at Ornan’s threshing floor.
easy.q: Where was David commanded to build an altar?

answers: Money only
The threshing floor and the materials for the offerings
The angel’s sword
easy.explanation: Ornan offered the place, the oxen, the threshing instruments, and the wheat.
easy.q: What did Ornan offer to give David?

answers: Rain
Smoke
Fire
easy.explanation: The LORD answered David from heaven by fire upon the altar.
easy.q: What came down from heaven upon the altar of burnt offering?

answers: He would not offer to the LORD something that belonged to another man
Ornan refused to give him anything
He wanted to purchase Jerusalem
medium.explanation: David said he would not take what was Ornan’s or offer burnt offerings without cost.
medium.q: Why did David insist on buying Ornan’s threshing floor for the full price?

answers: He built an altar and offered burnt offerings and peace offerings
He numbered the people again
He immediately left the place
medium.explanation: David built an altar, offered sacrifices, and called upon the LORD.
medium.q: What did David do after going up to the threshing floor?

answers: With only a partial payment
With complete payment
With payment at a later time
medium.explanation: David insisted on paying the complete value of the place.
medium.q: What does “for the full price” mean?

answers: David wanted the place so he could build an altar and seek the plague’s end
Ornan stopped the plague himself
The plague ended before David reached the threshing floor
challenge.explanation: David asked for the place so that he could build an altar and that the plague might be stayed.
challenge.q: What connection is shown between purchasing the place and stopping the plague?

answers: Ornan wanted to sell everything, but David refused
Ornan offered a gift, but David wanted to pay for his offering to the LORD
Both men refused to let the place be used for an altar
challenge.explanation: Ornan offered the place and materials freely, but David insisted on paying the full price.
challenge.q: What is shown by the contrast between Ornan’s offer and David’s insistence?

answers: The LORD answered David after he offered the sacrifices
The angel returned to destroy Jerusalem
The census had been accepted as sinless
challenge.explanation: After David built the altar and offered sacrifices, the LORD answered him from heaven by fire.
challenge.q: What does the fire from heaven signify in the sequence of events?

answers: At Ornan’s threshing floor
At Gibeon
In Israel’s camp

answers: In Jerusalem
At Gibeon
At Ornan’s threshing floor
easy.explanation: The passage says that the tabernacle and the altar of burnt offering were at Gibeon.

Joab prevented him from going
The tabernacle was no longer there

easy.q: Why could David not go to Gibeon to inquire of God?

answers: He sacrificed there
He assembled the tabernacle
He counted Levi and Benjamin
medium.explanation: Because the LORD had answered him at Ornan’s threshing floor, David sacrificed there.
medium.q: What did David do at the threshing floor after the LORD answered him?

Gibeon had no place for worship, while Ornan’s site had the tabernacle
Neither place had an altar
medium.explanation: The tabernacle and altar were at Gibeon, while David received the LORD’s answer at Ornan’s threshing floor.
medium.q: What is the main contrast between Gibeon and Ornan’s threshing floor?

answers: Calm
Frightened
Victorious
medium.explanation: David was frightened by the sword of the angel of the LORD.
medium.q: What does the word “afraid” mean in the statement that David was afraid because of the angel’s sword?

answers: The LORD had answered him at Ornan’s threshing floor
The people of Gibeon had closed the tabernacle
Joab commanded him to remain there
challenge.explanation: The passage connects David’s sacrifice at the threshing floor with the LORD’s answer there.
challenge.q: Why did David continue to worship at Ornan’s threshing floor even though the tabernacle was at Gibeon?

answers: He had not seen the angel
The vision and judgment still affected him
He opposed the worship of God
challenge.explanation: David’s fear of the sword kept him from going to Gibeon to inquire of God.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from David’s fear of the angel’s sword?

answers: Worship continued at Gibeon, but David acted at Ornan’s threshing floor after receiving God’s answer there
Ornan’s threshing floor replaced Gibeon for every matter in Israel
David abolished the tabernacle and the altar at Gibeon
challenge.explanation: The verses identify Gibeon as the location of the tabernacle and altar while explaining David’s worship at Ornan’s threshing floor.
challenge.q: How do the final verses summarize the relationship between Gibeon and Ornan’s threshing floor?
